pharm: Chimeric (murine/human) monoclonal antibody that binds the alpha (CD25) chain of the IL-2 receptor, providing induction immunosuppression to prevent acute rejection in renal transplantation.
quick: 20 mg IV pre-transplant + 20 mg IV on day 4 (two doses)
Use only if benefit justifies fetal risk; effective contraception required
summary: Basiliximab (Simulect) is a chimeric IL-2 receptor antagonist used for prophylaxis of acute organ rejection in renal transplant patients, given with cyclosporine and corticosteroids. It is administered as two fixed IV doses (pre-operatively and on day 4). Severe acute hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis can occur. It should be used only under the supervision of physicians experienced in immunosuppression and organ transplantation.
indications: Prophylaxis of acute organ rejection in patients receiving renal transplantation, as part of an immunosuppressive regimen including cyclosporine and corticosteroids

dosage.t: First dose within 2 hours before transplant surgery; second dose 4 days after transplantation
dosage.n: Withhold second dose if severe hypersensitivity or graft loss occurs

dosage.t: First dose within 2 hours pre-transplant; second dose 4 days post-transplant

admin: Reconstitute 10 mg vial with 2.5 mL and 20 mg vial with 5 mL Sterile Water for Injection
Give as an IV bolus or as an IV infusion over 20-30 minutes
First dose should not be given unless the patient is certain to receive the graft and concomitant immunosuppression
Have agents for treating severe hypersensitivity reactions immediately available
Administer under supervision of a transplant specialist
moa: Functions as an IL-2 receptor antagonist by binding with high affinity to the alpha (CD25) chain of the IL-2 receptor complex on activated T-lymphocytes, competitively inhibiting IL-2-mediated activation and clonal proliferation of lymphocytes - a critical step in the cellular immune response to allograft rejection.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to basiliximab or any component of the formulation
relative: Reexposure (prior basiliximab use increases hypersensitivity risk)

preg: Use only when the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception before, during, and for 4 months after therapy.
lact: It is not known whether basiliximab is excreted in human milk; because of potential for serious adverse reactions, weigh benefits against risks.
renal: No specific dose adjustment for renal impairment; used in the renal transplant population.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment for hepatic impairment.

major: Other potent immunosuppressants increase overall immunosuppression and infection/malignancy risk
moderate: No dose adjustment required when combined with cyclosporine, corticosteroids, azathioprine, or mycophenolate mofetil
minor: Compatible with ATG/ALG and muromonab-CD3 regimens

emergency: Severe acute hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis (hypotension, tachycardia, dyspnea, bronchospasm, pulmonary edema, respiratory failure)

monitoring: Signs of acute hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis during and after infusion
Signs of lymphoproliferative disease or malignancy
counsel: This medication is given by a transplant specialist to help prevent rejection of your new kidney
Report immediately any difficulty breathing, swelling, rash, or feeling faint during or after the infusion
Use effective contraception during and for 4 months after therapy
You are at increased risk of infection and certain cancers; report fever or new symptoms
Keep all transplant follow-up appointments and blood tests
pk: IL-2 receptor blockade immediate after infusion
Cmax ~7.1 mg/L after 20 mg IV infusion
pearls: Fixed dosing - no titration, two doses only (pre-op and day 4 post-op)
Provides induction immunosuppression without the cytokine-release syndrome seen with depleting antibodies
Risk of severe hypersensitivity is higher on re-exposure - withhold the second dose if a severe reaction occurs
Restricted to use by physicians experienced in transplantation and immunosuppression
No premedication routinely required, but anaphylaxis treatment must be available
missed: Doses are scheduled around surgery and on day 4; if the second dose schedule is disrupted, the transplant team determines timing. Withhold the second dose if severe hypersensitivity or graft loss occurs.
overdose: Maximum tolerated dose not determined; doses up to 120 mg divided over 3-5 days have been given without serious adverse events. Manage supportively and monitor for hypersensitivity and infection.
